text:
marcos: noticed a repeating memory "curve" on kv-shard-prod-3 — residency climbs steadily after ~12-20h and then OOMs during high write bursts. looks different from the big leak last year but still worrying. posting graphs: https://dash.redwood/graphs/kv-shard-prod-3/residency-week

tess: can you share allocation diffs? is fragmentation trending up or is it pure resident growth?

marcos: quick snapshot:
```
residency: 980M -> 1.45G over 16h
slab_frag_pct: 18% -> 38%
active_objects_count: +22% (mostly 16-64KB buckets)
```

jin: hmm 16-64KB buckets spiking suggests either batched writes or coalesced allocations. any recent change to batch size or chunking?

anya: we rolled `batcher.max_batch_size` from 8 -> 32 two deploys ago. could be related. I'm +1 for a temporary throttle and a reproducibility run with old/new batcher settings.

marcos: agreed. proposal: 1) canary rollback to batcher.max_batch_size=8 on 10% of nodes 2) enable nightly slab-compaction cron on non-prod and add a one-off compaction on the canary 3) add metric `kv.residency.slope_1h` and alert if > 70MB/hr 4) schedule deeper perf session to capture heap diffs during climb.

tess: sounds good. for compaction cron i can sketch a job:
```
# run on staging and canary-prod weekly
0 4 * * * /opt/redwood/bin/slab-compact --shard $SHARD --max-duration=300
```

jin: i'll own the perf session. timeline: 48h to reproduce with variant loads, collect `perf` + heap-diff + slab histograms. will test both batch sizes and also a patched allocator that forces immediate coalescing off-path.

anya: ops action: put a soft throttle at 1.25G residency per-shard with 5% canary rollout, throttle policy = shed-writes until residency < 1.1G. who should run the rollout?

marcos: can you handle the rollout? i'll monitor graphs.

ops-bot: runbook action queued: apply soft_residency_limit=1250MB -> canary 5% at 02:00 UTC by marcos. alerts: `kv.residency.slope_1h > 70MB` and `kv.error.rate > 0.5%`

marcos: reminder checklist for jin: 1) reproduce with `scripts/stress_kv.sh --batch-size=32 --concurrency=200 --duration=6h` 2) collect `heapdiff` every 30m 3) upload slab histograms to artifact store 4) test rollback to batch-size=8 and repeat.

jin: starting run now on staging. script: `scripts/stress_kv.sh --batch-size=$B --concurrency=200 --kv-size=16k --duration=6h` will post link to artifacts.

tess: i'll add `slab_fragmentation_pct` and `residency_slope_1h` to the shard dashboard and set a 24/7 alert with lower severity for the slope metric so we get early signal.

anya: longer-term options to consider after we have prof data: - eager per-key eviction after threshold - shard-level compact-on-idle - change batcher pacing to prefer smaller batches for hot prefixes - opportunistic background GC sweeping backpointer maps

marcos: decision log: immediate -> soft_residency_limit canary + rollback, perf reproduction & slab histograms (jin), instrumentation + dashboard updates (tess), nightly compaction trial on staging (tess). owners: jin(lead), tess(instrumentation), marcos(ops rollout), anya(product checks). aim to have root cause and prioritized fixes in 7 days.

jin: posting first perf artifacts in ~6h. curious if anyone can review a small allocator probe patch when ready (will tag @tess).

tess: will review. also will add a smoke-test job that runs `scripts/stress_kv.sh --batch-size=32 --concurrency=50 --duration=30m` nightly against staging and fails the build if residency slope > 40MB/hr.

ops-bot: smoke job scheduled: nightly-staging-kv-residency at 03:30 UTC. failure will open incident stub in #incidents and notify oncall.
